races.name: Simply Safe Care Group Handicap

runners_data.name: La Belle Forest
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning from 56-day break with solid 5f form but underwhelming handicap debut
runners_data.comment: Improved with each run and latest C&D win was a comfortable one; can do better
runners_data.spotlight: Ran in these colours for Karl Burke and was progressing when winning her AW maiden; her handicap debut back at Southwell was underwhelming given she went off favourite; probably better than that.

runners_data.name: Arctic Wind
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who was gelded before last start and may improve for David Evans
runners_data.comment: Makes his stable/handicap/AW debut after seven months off; market should be informative
runners_data.spotlight: Promising runs for David Menuisier whom he left for 9,000gns; gelded ahead of stable debut at Wolverhampton where he was beaten 7l in a small field; may have needed that after a lengthy break and there are races in him.

runners_data.name: Guernsey Lady
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in good form after close third at Bath following 142-day absence
runners_data.comment: Inconsistent filly who has a record of 1-11; comes with risks attached on return
runners_data.spotlight: Good-ground novice winner last year; not her first placing in handicap company when a close third at Bath two weeks ago after 142 days off; possibilities.

runners_data.name: Alkuwarrior
runners_data.note: Front-runner with poor 1-11 record but trying cheekpieces for first time
runners_data.comment: Finished last on both starts for this yard and has plenty to prove on his first go at 6f
runners_data.spotlight: Record of 1-11 overall; has finished last in two sprint handicaps for current yard; cheekpieces added.

runners_data.name: Arishka's Dream
runners_data.note: Prominent type in good AW form but went too fast on turf debut at Ripon
runners_data.comment: 6f Wolverhampton maiden winner; twice narrowly beaten since; merits respect on turf debut.
runners_data.spotlight: Bang in form on the AW before going off too fast when made favourite for his turf debut in a 6f handicap at Ripon; remains of interest and looks sharp enough for 5f; gelded since.

runners_data.name: Tie Fighter
runners_data.note: Hold-up seven-race maiden making handicap debut with first-time headgear
runners_data.comment: Chance largely depends on the effects of first-time headgear
runners_data.spotlight: Seven-race maiden who is making belated handicap debut; chance of opening his account largely depends on the effects of first-time headgear.

runners_data.name: Carefree Dream
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won soft-ground handicap but uncompetitive in two runs since
runners_data.spotlight: Won small-field 5f handicap on soft ground last September; uncompetitive in two runs since on either side of a break.

runners_data.name: Beach Partee
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse trying visor for first time after fairly close fifth at Bath
runners_data.spotlight: Three wins for William Knight last autumn; might be on the way back after a fairly close fifth at Bath when just behind Guernsey Lady.

races.paceDynamic: La Belle Forest and Alkuwarrior will dispute the early lead in this 5f handicap, with both confirmed front-runners likely to engage from the start. Arctic Wind, Guernsey Lady, Arishka's Dream and Carefree Dream should track close behind this pace, while Tie Fighter and Beach Partee will need to be produced from off the pace. The early battle between the two leaders should create an honest gallop that will test stamina over this minimum trip. This pace setup strongly favours prominent racers who can sit close to the pace without getting embroiled in the early battle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If La Belle Forest and Alkuwarrior duel early and weaken
scenarios.body: The pace battle sets this up perfectly for the prominent runners to strike in the final furlong. Arctic Wind, Guernsey Lady and Arishka's Dream are ideally positioned to capitalise on the leaders' exertions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If La Belle Forest gets first run on Alkuwarrior and kicks clear
scenarios.body: La Belle Forest's class edge shows as she breaks the dual and holds off late challengers. Her higher RPR of 80 and previous 5f form gives her the tools to complete wire-to-wire success.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Success
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is stronger than expected and leaders tire badly
scenarios.body: Tie Fighter and Beach Partee benefit from a collapse up front with both sporting headgear for the first time. The pace meltdown allows the hold-up horses to pick up the pieces despite their modest recent form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Alkuwarrior Shock
scenarios.trigger: If the cheekpieces transform Alkuwarrior and he outkicks La Belle Forest
scenarios.body: The headgear sparks improvement in the Christopher Mason runner who uses his lead to devastating effect. His 1-11 record suggests this is unlikely but the equipment change could be the catalyst needed.

watchPoints.text: La Belle Forest could be vulnerable after 56 days off and disappointing last handicap run
Watch if Alkuwarrior shows early pace with the cheekpieces as this could set up a stronger gallop
Tie Fighter and Beach Partee both have first-time headgear which could spark improvement
Arishka's Dream went too fast last time on turf so jockey tactics will be crucial
Arctic Wind was gelded before his last run and this could be his first start showing the benefit

runners_data.name: Another Encore
runners_data.spotlight: 60,000gns yearling; third foal; dam placed 1m2f/1m3f in France (RPR 71), sister to smart 1m1f/1m2f winner Collins Street; in good hands and this isn't a strong race, so would be tempting if prominent in the betting.

runners_data.name: Galipi
runners_data.spotlight: 72,000gns yearling; fifth foal; half-brother to four winners including Zillow (11.5f/1m4f Flat, RPR 92; useful 2m hurdle), Genetique (French 6.5f) and Energic (French 9.5f-1m4f); dam French 1m1f winner; bred to win races and the market can guide.

runners_data.name: Sea Idol
runners_data.comment: Gelded son of Sea The Moon; a watching brief is advised unless betting hints otherwise
runners_data.spotlight: 75,000gns gelded son of Sea The Moon; went off 28-1 at Southwell (7f AW) but his late rally saw him go down by only a head; given the stable he represents, it's realistic to expect better again this evening.

runners_data.name: Real Trouble
runners_data.spotlight: Cost 105,000gns and already gelded; only weakened late on when beaten under 4l at Newcastle (6f) and improvement looks on the cards now raised to 7f; good chance according to RPRs.

runners_data.name: Alfey Moon
runners_data.comment: March foal; dam won on her May juvenile debut; watch for market interest on this first go
runners_data.spotlight: 33-1 and was tenth of the 12 runners on good to soft at Chepstow (6f); limited appeal on that performance.

runners_data.name: Persian Land
runners_data.comment: Trainer saddles two debutants; check the betting, but he may be best watched
runners_data.spotlight: Outpaced for a long way at Haydock (6f, soft; 14-1) but the leaders stopped and he won going away; could have been flattered but clearly has a fair level of ability and Jack Dace's claim takes care of much of the penalty.

runners_data.name: Le Ciel Noble
runners_data.comment: One of two newcomers for yard and market check is advised, but others make greater appeal
runners_data.spotlight: 40-1 and never seen with a chance at Haydock in the race won by stablemate Persian Land.

races.name: Pro Panther Handicap

runners_data.name: Opening Bat
runners_data.note: Prominent racer suited by the likely lack of early pressure, though 14 days since last run keeps him sharp for this distance drop.
runners_data.comment: Solid 3yo campaign & reappears with yard back among winners; player under Billy Loughnane
runners_data.spotlight: 1m AW winner off 1lb lower; also competitive in defeat and reportedly unsuited by the undulations of Chepstow when tailed off on his comeback, though good to soft may also have been a factor.

runners_data.name: Toralou
runners_data.note: Natural front runner who will dictate the pace without pressure, though David Probert must ensure fractions don't become too slow.
runners_data.comment: Has form figures of 26221 on turf; return to this sphere is the angle with her
runners_data.spotlight: Much better record on turf than AW, though one she failed to enhance at Newbury 20 days ago; that was underwhelming.

runners_data.name: Nakaaha
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs the pace to develop into a genuine test, with the sustainable early fractions potentially working against her style.
runners_data.comment: Scored at Ffos Las and Newbury last summer; runner-up at Bath last month.
runners_data.spotlight: Won over 1m at Newbury and here last summer; up and down this season and the recent rain was probably no help.

runners_data.name: Devious Devan
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who fades in the finish but could benefit from the uncontested early pace, though 30 days off raises fitness questions.
runners_data.spotlight: Hurled in on what he achieved as a 3yo and belatedly returned to form when a length winner at Wolverhampton (8.6f; backed into 9-2); raised just 3lb and he has form here.

runners_data.name: Thiscouldbefun
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 167 days off but Ashley Lewis's 5lb claim helps significantly in a race lacking early pace.
runners_data.comment: Two 1m wins this year; only 6th behind Towerlands 11 days ago; needs a career best to win
runners_data.spotlight: Two 1m wins last year, on the AW and good to firm (handles soft); off since December but could have a big run in her with Ashley Lewis taking off 5lb.

runners_data.name: Grey Soul
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs strong pace to set up his finishing kick, with the lack of early pressure potentially leaving him too much to do.
runners_data.spotlight: Signed off for Roger Varian with a victory at Newcastle (1m AW) in first-time blinkers; shaped okay on yard debut when in no headgear at Kempton (1m) and could be a factor now tried in cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Auburn Avenue
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 218 days absence, needing the race to develop into a test of stamina rather than early positioning.
runners_data.spotlight: Left Ireland for 15,000euros and a 15-race maiden, though very nearly put that right on the AW (1m) in October; has turf form as well; could be interesting on stable debut should market vibes be at all posititive.

runners_data.name: Sea The Light
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in cheekpieces who has struggled in recent handicaps and needs significant pace pressure to be effective.
runners_data.spotlight: Debut winner who hasn't offered a great deal in four handicaps over longer distances, latterly in cheekpieces (reapplied) and blinkers; bit risky.

runners_data.name: Mereside Madness
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in tongue-tie who has been regressing and faces an unfavourable race shape for his running style.
runners_data.spotlight: A four-time winner but has been regressing for a while and no effort of note for current yard.

runners_data.name: Eagle Day
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who fades in finish and seems much better on all-weather, with the eyeshield representing a last resort.
runners_data.spotlight: His 8.6f win at Wolverhampton came out of the blue and he then disappointed at Nottingham; seems far more effective on the AW; tries an eyeshield.

runners_data.name: Orchard
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 357 days off with best form on all-weather, making this turf return after a year highly questionable.
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win and best form has been on the AW, and it's nearly a year since he finished last in a Newbury handicap (1m); perhaps best watched.

runners_data.name: Norflondonforever
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in cheekpieces returning from long absence but faces a pace scenario that could suit his natural style.
runners_data.comment: 5 races; first tongue-tie when winning at Kempton (1m, AW) last April by a head; off since
runners_data.spotlight: Won over Kempton's AW 1m in April of last year; not seen again until this May when tailed off at Haydock (1m2f, good to soft); cheekpieces added.

runners_data.name: Sixfiveseven
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in blinkers who showed improvement last time and needs the pace to develop into a genuine staying test.
runners_data.spotlight: Newmarket winner in late 2024 (1m, good; fine on soft); second run back from a long absence was better than the first and he might progress again; realistic mark.

races.paceDynamic: Toralou will take the field along as the only confirmed front runner, with Opening Bat, Devious Devan, Thiscouldbefun and Norflondonforever sitting prominent. The absence of early pace pressure means Toralou can dictate fractions without being hustled, creating a sustainable rhythm that builds gradually. This sets up a race where the leaders can maintain their positions without burning energy, while the hold-up horses like Nakaaha, Grey Soul, Auburn Avenue and Sea The Light face the challenge of making up ground against horses who haven't been softened up. The race shape strongly favours prominent racers and front runners who can secure good positions without early pressure.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustainable Pace Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Toralou sets uncontested fractions and the prominent horses travel kindly
scenarios.body: The leaders maintain their advantage as hold-up horses struggle to make meaningful inroads against horses who haven't been weakened by early pace pressure. Front runners and prominent racers dominate the finish with their positional advantage intact.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Kick Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly dawdling and turns into a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure test of acceleration over the final two furlongs, suiting horses with sharp finishing kicks regardless of early position. Hold-up horses get their ideal scenario with a genuine late surge deciding the outcome.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pressure Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Opening Bat and others pressure Toralou more than expected in the early stages
scenarios.body: The pace quickens enough to compromise the front division but not enough for a complete collapse, creating an advantage for horses sitting just off the pace. Mid-division runners who can pick up the pieces benefit most.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Toralou gets completely uncontested fractions and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace pressure allows the front runner to build an unassailable lead, with the field struggling to respond to the sustained drive. Only other prominent racers have any chance of getting close.

watchPoints.text: Toralou could get uncontested fractions that prove impossible to peg back, especially if David Probert misjudges the pace and goes too slowly early.
Opening Bat and other prominent horses may not apply enough early pressure to Toralou, creating a tactical disadvantage for hold-up horses.
Thiscouldbefun returns from 167 days off but Ashley Lewis's claim could be crucial in a race where every pound matters from prominent positions.
Grey Soul and other hold-up horses need to be prominent early if the pace becomes as sustainable as expected, or they'll have too much ground to make up.
Auburn Avenue and Orchard both return from very long absences and may need this run more than showing their true ability first time back.

races.name: New Thomas Arms Handicap

runners_data.name: Salkadan
runners_data.note: Recent handicap winner who could be well-treated and might get better position than usual given weak pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Much improved upped to 1m4f when second at Kempton; may still have untapped potential
runners_data.spotlight: Nearly won his first handicap and went one better in the second, albeit narrowly over a similar trip at Haydock (good); the runner-up was disappointing last weekend but this 3yo only went up 2lb and looks progressive.

runners_data.name: Kelly Burn
runners_data.note: Recent AW winner stepping up in class but proven over trip with strong finishing kick suited to tactical affair
runners_data.comment: Ran well when favourite over C&D last month; there should be more to come from her.
runners_data.spotlight: Has improved for handicaps and edged home in a small field at Wolverhampton (1m4f AW); only 2lb higher now but in what looks a better race.

runners_data.name: Al's River
runners_data.note: Fitted with first-time blinkers which could provide needed inspiration for previously disappointing handicap efforts
runners_data.spotlight: Improved in last season's novice races at about 1m but it's been a low-key start in handicaps, at 1m2f and 1m3f; trainer turns to blinkers for some inspiration.

runners_data.name: Willow Wood
runners_data.note: Expensive purchase underperforming her breeding but conditions might suit if jockey shows tactical awareness early
runners_data.comment: Well-bred filly; showed only minor promise as a 2yo but ought to improve this year
runners_data.spotlight: 200,000gns 2yo who is bred to be better than this mark but she was beaten about 6l in her first handicap over 1m2f on the AW; has to improve on that effort but it's still relatively early days.

runners_data.name: Eze Sur Mer
runners_data.note: Showed little in three starts and beaten badly on handicap debut, hard to recommend in competitive heat
runners_data.comment: Began career with two fairly encouraging AW runs; well beaten on turf since
runners_data.spotlight: Not that dangerous in her first three races and again when 33-1 for handicap debut at Redcar (1m2f); wouldn't be the obvious answer.

runners_data.name: Brave Leader
runners_data.note: Disappointed as favorite on handicap debut but Tom Ward stable in poor form recently with 0/4 record
runners_data.comment: Steady improver last term; pedigree says this trip helps on h'cap debut/return; gelded
runners_data.spotlight: Steady improvement last year and appeared to perform below expectations on his handicap debut at Doncaster (1m2f, good to firm; 9-4 favourite); interest to see if backers return.

runners_data.name: Reem Rak
runners_data.note: Strong second at Newcastle reads well but failed to fire when favorite on handicap debut in April
runners_data.spotlight: The form of her second at Newcastle last season reads well (7f AW) and she couldn't have given her true running when made favourite for handicap debut in April (1m); could be given another chance and she's bred for this far.

runners_data.name: Mick The Hat
runners_data.note: Beaten badly in qualifying races but significant weight relief and trip increase could transform prospects
runners_data.comment: Safely held in all three qualifying races but should be more competitive on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten at least 12l in three qualifying races (1m-8.6f) but now goes handicapping at a modest level and over a longer trip; the market could tell a tale.

runners_data.name: Aravalli
runners_data.note: New to stable after Irish purchase and likely to get uncontested lead as only front runner in field
runners_data.comment: Beaten 20l at Leopardstown and 24l at the Curragh, much more needed
runners_data.spotlight: Showed more on third and final run in Irish maidens, finishing fourth of ten at Cork (1m2f, soft); left Jessica Harrington for 22,000gns; likely best watched unless backed.

races.paceDynamic: Aravalli is the only confirmed front runner and should get an uncontested lead in this small field of hold-up horses. With eight runners all showing hold-up tendencies, there will be minimal early pressure allowing Aravalli to dictate fractions. The lack of prominent runners means the field will be bunched behind the leader with most making their moves from off the pace in the straight. This tactical setup strongly favors front runners and any horse that can secure an early position, as the hold-up brigade will face traffic problems and need significant pace bias to succeed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Aravalli gets soft fractions and stays on strongly
scenarios.body: The sole pace-setter controls the race from the front and proves hard to peg back when the hold-up horses make their late moves. Front runners and any horse that can secure an early position benefit from the lack of early pace pressure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Finisher Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The crawling early pace sets up a furlong dash where the best turn of foot wins regardless of position. Superior class horses with proven finishing kicks thrive in this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Mover Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one runner positions prominently early behind Aravalli
scenarios.body: A tactical runner breaks from the pack earlier than the rest and gets first run on the leader while others are still organizing their challenges. Horses whose jockeys show initiative gain crucial positioning advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Bias Swing
scenarios.trigger: If the ground rides slower than expected favoring deep closers
scenarios.body: Late runners get maximum assistance from conditions and the hold-up style becomes an advantage rather than hindrance. The deepest held horses with strongest finishing kicks benefit most.

watchPoints.text: Aravalli getting soft early fractions as the only pace-setter could prove decisive in this tactical affair
Kelly Burn and Salkadan both proven recent winners who could be underestimated in what looks a competitive handicap
Al's River wearing first-time blinkers after disappointing handicap starts could show significant improvement
The ground conditions staying truly good as any softening would heavily favor the deeper held runners
Mick The Hat receiving 15lbs from top weight despite modest form could be live outsider if step up in trip helps

races.name: Go Maintenance Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Adrian
runners_data.note: Hold-up 9yo with 38 days off who won Group 3 in Germany but has been regressive and probably wants 2m
runners_data.comment: Back from break on career-low mark but has not won since 2021; difficult to enthuse over
runners_data.spotlight: A regressive 9yo who last won in 2021, a 1m4f Group 3 in Germany; well beaten after a break and probably wants 2m ideally.

runners_data.name: Change Of Fortune
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with poor 1-36 strike rate but possible at 1m4f after reasonable classified effort
runners_data.spotlight: Strike-rate of 1-36 but not had many chances at 1m4f over which he was beaten 3l in a classified race on the AW last time; possible.

runners_data.name: Buck Barrow
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose sole win came here on good-to-soft but struggling this season with 13 days since last run
runners_data.comment: Below form lately; raced freely when behind here on sole go beyond 1m4f (1m5f last year)
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win came in 1m2f handicap here last June on good to soft; below par this season but the recent rain heightens interest.

runners_data.name: Hedonista
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who is 0-11 for current yard and essentially regressive with massive 135-day layoff
runners_data.spotlight: Dual winner but 0-11 for current yard and essentially regressive; off since January.

runners_data.name: Belle Amie
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won 1m4f classified race on debut for new yard Simcock and appeals most given tactical advantage
runners_data.comment: Winning start for David Simcock at Wolverhampton in February; must enter calculations
runners_data.spotlight: Consistent maiden for David Menuisier; won a 1m4f classified race on her debut for this yard and then ran pretty well in a Windsor handicap; appeals most.

runners_data.name: Highland Harvey
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with fade-in-finish warning but was competitive in similar races before 109-day break
runners_data.comment: Ex-Irish maiden; fair 2nd in 0-50 on his stable debut on Monday; chance if building on it
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-Irish maiden; competitive in two 1m4f races (classified/handicap) for Denis Quinn; shouldn't be far away in similar form after a break.

runners_data.name: Oceanides
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with poor BHA mark of 23 and fade-in-finish warning from bumper/AW form
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in two starts on the Flat at this track; others preferred
runners_data.spotlight: Poor form in a bumper and three runs on the AW at up to 9.4f; has a BHA mark of 23.

runners_data.name: Lamlash
runners_data.note: Sole front runner who has never beaten a rival on Flat but will get uncontested lead with sustainable pace
runners_data.spotlight: Pulled up in one hurdle start and has yet to beat a rival on the Flat, including a handicap.

races.paceDynamic: Lamlash is the only confirmed front runner and will lead uncontested from the start, setting a sustainable pace over this 1m4f trip. Belle Amie will likely track prominently from her P style, while the majority of the field (Adrian, Change Of Fortune, Buck Barrow, Hedonista, Highland Harvey, Oceanides) are hold-up merchants who will settle towards the back. With minimal early pressure on Lamlash and a large pack of closers, this sets up a tactical affair with a strong kick required in the final 3f. This race shape clearly favours prominent runners and those with proven finishing pace over pure hold-up horses who may get caught in traffic.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lamlash leads throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Lamlash maintains his lead and the pace stays steady without early pressure.
scenarios.body: The uncontested leader gets first run on the field while the large pack of hold-up horses struggle to organize their challenge in time. Front runners and prominent racers benefit from avoiding the inevitable traffic problems behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent closer prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Belle Amie or another prominent runner can position perfectly and unleash a strong finish.
scenarios.body: The tactical nature allows those racing handily to avoid trouble while still having enough punch to reel in Lamlash's moderate gallop. Belle Amie's recent yard switch success and prominent style fits perfectly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late hold-up surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race and Lamlash fades, opening the door for a strong closer.
scenarios.body: Highland Harvey or Change Of Fortune could benefit from a stronger gallop that sets up their preferred finishing kick. However, the sheer number of hold-up horses creates traffic concerns that may blunt several challenges.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise unconsidered winner
scenarios.trigger: If Adrian finds his old German Group 3 form or Buck Barrow responds to the good ground.
scenarios.body: An outsider capitalizes on the tactical nature and moderate pace to spring a surprise. The even weights and classified level creates opportunities for horses with hidden ability.

watchPoints.text: Highland Harvey and Change Of Fortune both have hold-up styles in a race packed with closers, creating serious traffic concerns
Lamlash has never beaten a rival on the Flat but gets an uncontested lead that could change his fortune
Belle Amie's prominent style gives her a tactical edge over the hold-up brigade and she's already won at this trip for new yard
Buck Barrow's headgear change to pacifiers suggests connections are trying something different after poor recent form
Adrian and Hedonista both return from long breaks (38d and 135d respectively) in a race requiring sharp finishing pace

races.name: New Thomas Arms Handicap

runners_data.name: Premier
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose best wins came wearing a hood which is absent today, creating form concerns despite decent recent efforts
runners_data.comment: Both wins came in a hood, which is absent as he returns from wind surgery
runners_data.spotlight: Both wins, including one over hurdles, came in a hood, which was absent when well beaten on the AW last month and again here; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Crackergee
runners_data.note: Inexperienced on turf as an 11-race maiden, headgear has been removed after disappointing recent efforts
runners_data.comment: 0-10; needs the longer trip and first-time cheekpieces to make a difference
runners_data.spotlight: 11-race maiden having only his third run on turf; yet to find his best form this season and the headgear tried last time is dispensed with.

runners_data.name: Mighty Quiet
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse returning from 57-day break with tongue-tie fitted, inconsistent but capable on her day
runners_data.comment: Has patchy record but she's a dual winner who needs a close look on her reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Effective on good and heavy; quiet comeback run and she can be inconsistent, but she's a dual winner on a fair mark and very capable at this level.

runners_data.name: Risen Again
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing cheekpieces, yet to show best form since stable change despite fair historical record
runners_data.comment: Failed to beat a rival in handicaps at Lingfield and Bath in 2026; others appeal more
runners_data.spotlight: A fair 1m2f winner at his best but yet to run a race of note since leaving Alice Haynes.

runners_data.name: Zambezi Magic
runners_data.note: Veteran who relishes soft conditions and this track, wears a hood and could surprise after 69-day absence
runners_data.spotlight: Ran okay after a break on the AW and he loves it here, especially when the mud is flying; the recent rain has helped his cause no end.

runners_data.name: Ghost Story
runners_data.note: Best recent form horse with strong finishing kick, returning from AW reappearance in good order
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced and her two wins have been over 1m2f on good to soft and soft; perhaps a tad high in the weights but her AW reappearance was respectable and this scenario suits her better.

races.paceDynamic: With all six runners classified as hold-up horses and no natural front-runners, this race will likely unfold at a crawling early pace with jockeys reluctant to make the running. Someone will be forced to lead reluctantly, probably Mighty Quiet or Ghost Story, but the pace will be pedestrian through the early stages. The real race begins when they quicken turning for home, creating a sprint finish over the final 3-4 furlongs. This tactical scenario strongly favours horses with the best finishing kick and those who can quicken sharply from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Crawling Pace Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow with no horse willing to commit early
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint finish where class and turn of foot decide the outcome. Ghost Story and Mighty Quiet benefit most from being able to unleash their best finishing efforts.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Moderate Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If one horse decides to take them along at a reasonable clip from the start
scenarios.body: The steadier tempo allows all runners to get competitive but still creates opportunities for closers with good acceleration. Risen Again and Premier can capitalize on their hold-up style when given something to aim at.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Traffic Issues
scenarios.trigger: If the slow pace leads to a bunched field causing interference in the straight
scenarios.body: Horses drawn wide or those that get clear runs benefit significantly over those trapped on the rails. Positioning and luck become crucial factors, potentially allowing outsiders like Crackergee to sneak through.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Early Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Zambezi Magic or Premier unexpectedly makes the running and sustains it
scenarios.body: The honest gallop plays to stamina rather than pure speed, suiting horses who stay this trip well. This tactical shift could expose the pure sprinters while benefiting genuine stayers.

watchPoints.text: Watch for traffic problems in the straight as all six runners will be coming from the back, creating potential interference
Monitor the early pace carefully as no natural leader could result in an extremely slow gallop favouring pure speed horses
Ghost Story's positioning will be crucial given her best recent form and need for a clear run in the final furlong
Mighty Quiet's fitness after 57 days off may be exposed if this becomes a searching test
Watch for any horse that breaks the mould and goes forward early, as they could steal a march on the field
